issue.title: Decide how memory task beads under %auto obtain human consent for memory decisions

task_type_fields.proposal: Memory task beads worked through `sase bead work` under %auto can never get a verified human consent for a memory decision. Their phase/task prompts are agent-written, so the plan's `requested:` quote never verifies, every memory decision clamps to off, and the memory change is filed as a follow-up again. Decide between (a) never auto-approving plans launched from `memory` task beads, so a human answers the memory decision in review, or (b) counting a human-created bead's description/title as human-authored text in sdd/plan_human_text.py (provenance-checked by bead creator).
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: This is a policy decision for Bryan about consent semantics. It goes beyond the Plan Decisions epic's fail-closed provenance contract (plan section 4), which deliberately counts only typed prompts, human feedback, and human Q&A text. Proposed by sase-1hi.9 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #4).

issue.creation_reason: Under Plan Decisions' fail-closed provenance, memory task beads worked under %auto can never switch a memory decision on, so the memory edit they exist for is always deferred.
